Title: New Widget editor
Description: Main User Benefit : Simplify widget creation / edition thanks to a wysiwyg editor - Visual editor for the creation of widgets from scratch - Library of ready to use widgets: pop-in, banners, countdown banner... - Easy management of created widget, with a widget dashboard page - Update of the logic we associate widgets in campaigns ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/10a0c54592bc8f5924a326d97bc9e31147da4b8c17f75909f092e3168e89ddb2/10A.jpg) ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/c65d02042d0ea3d74f505f6045fac319ceb8910e6ba42ca4ecdae06e7c3ea2dc/Type_of_creation_(1).jpeg) **Hypothesis driving this project** Marketers do not see the value of our existing widget library (and to some extend our personalization module) because widgets cannot be easily customized to their needs, so we expect that solving this problem will increase the overall satisfaction of customers with our Personalization module and increase our ability to convince marketers users during sales speech. **Metric(s) and Baseline: How we will evaluate success** Baseline: number of predefined widgets used in production / month Metrics to measure when the feature is released: 1. Number of widgets created 2. NPS satisfaction measured for personalization customers (Appcues NPS for personalization customers only) 3. Win rate against AB Tasty thanks to the new widget graphic editor **Business Impact** - We expect to upsell more existing A/B testing customers to the Personalization module - We expect to increase our winning rate against A/B Tasty **Problem Statement. What pain point(s) are we trying to address?** - Today we provide a library of predefined widgets for marketers and a code-based editor to build custom widgets for developers. However, marketers can not simply create new widgets (eg. popin or banner) or adapt our existing widgets to their needs because we do not provide the right user experience or the right tools for that, so we expect that solving this problem will increase the satisfaction among our existing customers and improve our sales performance (especially when we are against AB Tasty) **How do people currently solve this problem? How do our competitors address this problem?** - They mainly ask our professional team to build custom widgets (with code) - Some competitors (Dynamic Yield or AB Tasty) provide a graphic editor or well designed widgets that can be easily customizable. **What is the project type and our justification for doing this project?** - Requested capability among SMB customers with no access to a technical team. - Some customers churned by the past to AB Tasty because they offered a more adapted product to their needs. **Jobs to be done** P0 “Must have” - Graphic editor for Personalization customers only - library of predefined templates that a customer can use if he does not want to start from scratch P1 “Nice to have” - Module that can be added as an add-on to A/B testing only customers - Ability to generate a HTML view (to embed on a mobile app as a webview). Requested by BPCE Customer) and would make sense for mobile apps customers. Dynamic Yield provides this option. - Additional components (countdown, tooltip, newsletter popin..) **When do we expect to launch?** - End of January in production - A/B testing customers only will still be able to use the existing library of widgets. So no change/update for them.

I have to rely on the results of my pre\-prod QA to be assured that my release will not break anything major and consequently affect all of my user base\. I am also unable to plan for any sudden loads on bandwidth, storage or infrastructure when my new release is made public\. - **Existing workaround:** None\. Currently, users would have to create individual rollouts for each individual increment\. - **Justification:** A major selling point for some of our competitors\. Progressive rollouts are an established good practice and meets our audience's needs\. --- ## 💡 Solution - **Product package:** Full stack - **User roles**: PM, EM, QA, RM \- or anyone concerned with product\/version releases\. - **Product scope:** The option can be found in the right overlay when adding a new rule in the Rollout Planner\. All UI changes reside in the same overlay\. - **Product design:** Selecting this option will prompt the user to define a few parameters: 1. Choose Progressive rollout when adding a new rule ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/b019216e125aaf2aa9da9f80bc8f02128c11b7c2c3f91fb6ffdbddddbcb6b1c5/image.png) Then, in the next screen, fill in your parameters for progressive rollout: 1. Choose audience\/segment for this rule \(or create a new one\) 1. Start date 1. Initial exposure \(e\.g: 0%\) 1. Increment \(e\.g: 20%\) 1. Interval between increments \(e\.g: 5 days\) 1. Final exposure cap \(e\.g: 80%\) → Upon this final entry, the user sees an indication of when and at what exposure percentage the rollout will stop\. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/27fcda0472191b50264f4291e43a0b11159bf9fe4e8a84fa925327d9b464a06b/image.png) --- ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Market\-Fit:** This feature brings us on par with LaunchDarkly and Flagship, the only two competitors offering this functionality\. - **Adoption:** Once released, active customers try out progressive delivery at least once\. --- ## 📄 Attached documents - **Figma file**: [https:\/\/www\.figma\.com\/file\/b8VwBwFMilgBCTJUH7DRKe\/Hybrid\-Plan?node\-id=400%3A75886](https://www.figma.com/file/b8VwBwFMilgBCTJUH7DRKe/Hybrid-Plan?node-id=400%3A75886) - **Redmine ticket**:

Title: Sample ratio mismatch
Description: This feature would be a flag which would be raise if we detect that the statistical results we show might not be valid because the observed deviation between the reference and the variations are not what should be expected. One can read about it [here](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/experimentation-platform-exp/articles/diagnosing-sample-ratio-mismatch-in-a-b-testing/). Implementation wise it would be to a use a test such as a chi-square statistic to determine whether the observed distribution of users in experiment variants statistically differs from the one that was configured. To compute it we need the number of visits in the reference and in each variation and the expected deviation for this experiment. If the difference is significative p-value \< 0.0005) we raise the warning.

Title: Multiple testing correction method
Description: This correction helps against the [multiple comparisons problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_comparisons_problem) basically, as we increase the number of variation, we increase the number of test statistics being computed and doing so, we increase the probability of being wrong\. Saying otherwise, as we add more variation, it becomes increasingly likely that one variation appears as a reliable winner due to random sampling error alone\. To shield our customer from taking wrong conclusion we should implement a correction to the displayed reliability in case of multi\-variate testing \(it could be extended to goals in a second time\)\. A first very simple correction would be the Bonferroni one, where we simply multiply the p\-value by the number of variations\. A preferred and more advanced one would be the Holm\-Bonferroni one\. It requires to first sort all the p\-values of the tests, and then to multiply the smallest by the number of variations, the second smallest by the number of variation minus one etc\.

Title: Contentful Integration
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` The Contentful Integration allows Contentful users to run experiments on content directly from Contentful UI and use Kameleoon powerful analytics solution to analyse the performance of those experiments. ``` **What is Contentful ?** Contentful is a headless CMS, a composable content platform that meets the unique demands of digital content and all the teams that produce and work with it\. Built with an API\-first architecture, Contentful orchestrates content from multiple sources and publishes it to any digital channel\. It ensures content is discoverable and reusable, provides tailored interfaces, and incorporates governance through role\-based access management and workflows\. **What is a Headless content management system \(CMS\) ?** A headless CMS comprises three parts: a backend, APIs, and an interface\. The backend stores content and organizes data\. [APIs](https://www.contentful.com/blog/2015/10/22/contentful-a-content-platform/) connect the database to presentation layers\. These presentation layers are independent from the CMS and thus malleable\. Headless CMSes are defined by this lack of presentation layer\. \(If you were looking for it, this is the head in headless CMS\.\) Going headless allows you to distribute content through multiple channels on all sorts of platforms at scale\. ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Title: Create components to easily reuse any element anywhere
Description: **Use case :** It can be very useful to reuse a same element either in the same widget (in the same screen or on other screens) or even in other widgets. For example, if you create a multi screens widget, you might need to reuse a same button on each screen. **Solution proposed:** - From any screen of the "Design Tab", you can select any element and "Create a component" (clicking on the 3 dots icon) - Then, in the "Add element" section (on click on + icon), a new section "Components" appears, with the list of all components already defined. Choose on component of the section to add it to the screen being editied. - Later, if you decide to edit this component to update its design, all the changes will be applied for each instance of the component (in other words, you update the component only once, and the changes apply wherever the component is used) - If you want to apply a change only for a specific instance, you will be able to "Detach instance" (to make it independant from the component) This "Component" feature can save designers a lot of time when creating their screens.

Title: Rollout Summary
Description: This section provides a quick overview of 2 key aspects of your rollout rules: **variations** and **segments**\. Changing the order of cards, deleting a rule, or change of rule status from active to planned or vice versa will reflect the ordering and values inside summary cards\. While the summary section accounts for untargeted \(remaining users\) that can be passed down to the next rule, any partial or complete overlaps between different user segments across different rules will not be accounted for or identified\. ### Variations Summary: ![](https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/YflvPqumSLthuw9rl7-uTkv0WfbzgHkCw7tTH6xObHEphZnoV9etkYQFBNx6-zWUYOs2HOdyv4Jfx-mBNTojwHg-T1r4eZdPanB_x7N4xUyNwvaOhbIVGpMiXbNrbjOqVuU8ZMHSThGj50tKjiCt4jU) This section serves you an overview of which variations have been used in your delivery and experiment rules\. Variations that are targeting multiple segments have multiple bars inside them also displaying the percentage of the audience that you have targeted\. ### Segments Summary: ![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/8Ako-pIU01miFIrW5oBeRL0PajcwCgygeY7XLejKchVlLuH00qpErRO6-FbzX-lWdNwoRpdhgQZStAKfItXNBCe3HypLflMddaoSP8Xgmdzr3k3_Zv2xNWCO-g5WPdfEBWEcbEWgbysLoJz4axuw0Ws) This section summarizes the different user segments that are being targeted in your rollout rules\. Title: Engine - Sending queue messages
Description: For the engine part, we have two options: - Option 1 : The rebuild is successful \(we have a success status\), then we send a message in the queue \( `queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms` \) containing the sitecode\. This is what we are currently doing : we send a message \( through `queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms` \) to notify the CDN to purge the cache\. This action is triggered when the rebuild is successful\. - Option 2 : The rebuild respond with an OK\/KO status, then the engine will create a new queue \(like `queue-kameleoon-rebuild-status` \) and send an object containing the sitecode and the status\. This is what we can do if we would like to send a status with the sitecode, so this queue will be triggered whether the rebuild is successful or not \(compare to the `queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms` queue that is triggered only when the rebuild is successful, this is why there's no status in it\)\.

Title: Backend - Saving queue objects in the database
Description: On the backend side, we wait for the queue objects, and save them using the sitecode associated with the data as an array containing the date \(or the status in the case of option 2\)\. Done the same time as ADMIN BO\. [](https://project.kameleoon.net/issues/18240)

Logging ensures each action performed on Kameleoon can be linked back to individual users and thus ensure sanctity of daily operations 1. **Monitoring & Compliance:** Given the substantial overlap of DevOps with feature flagging, logs help find needles in a haystack, and subsequently make the software delivery cycle more secure and compliant 1. **Tech\. Debt Management:** A major challenge of working with feature flagging is the tech debt that accumulates over time\. Title: Automatic Rollbacks
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** This feature will allow users of FME to turn off a feature automatically if predefined KPI thresholds are met\. The user will be able to choose the KPIs that will act as triggers for the rollback, as well as the values at which the feature should turn off\. The user can also choose the minimum number of visitors evaluated or time elapsed before the rollback condition takes effect, as well as the option to notify themselves or others if a rollback occurs\. ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** - As a PM, dev or analyst, when I want to proactively turn off a poorly performing feature with minimal monitoring, there’s no way to set and forget\. - Even Progressive delivery rules, despite their slow ramp\-up, still need to be monitored manually\. - Implementing automatic feature rollbacks can be complex and time\-consuming, requiring significant effort to set up and maintain - I don’t have control over critical mass of customers to have been exposed before my guardrail takes action \(to ensure the rollback is not a false positive\) - I have to configure alerts from the results page and can only do so for experiments at the moment \- and the entire process is very disjoint from the creation step\. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Partially - **Workaround description:** Only for Feature Experiments ➜ Using the results page of experiments to create manual alerts for specific KPIs\. ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: 1. **Saves time and effort:** Automatic feature rollbacks save developers time and effort by automatically rolling back features that are causing issues or bugs, rather than having to manually identify and revert them\. 1. **Reduces downtime:** By quickly detecting and rolling back problematic features, automatic feature rollbacks can help reduce system downtime and minimize the impact on end\-users\. 1. **Improves stability:** By automatically detecting and rolling back problematic features, the overall stability of the system can be improved, reducing the likelihood of future issues\. **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management - **Product scope:** Inside rule configuration overlay - **Target Persona**: All - **Main updates:** - Additional step when creating or editing a rule\. - User selects parameters for triggering rollback and the minimum thresholds\. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/6d814765e3f1aaef1f4cf71292df26958e3e326bf6d4317e2381bb4197b91ba9/image.png) ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - Title: Raw visit/visitor export
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` Raw visit/visitor export allows every user to get the raw data of an experiment by adding the option to export the data "raw" in the "export" menu in the "Actions" dropdown, on the result page. ``` ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? ``` As a user, I can't currently get the data Kameleoon is collecting in order to display the result page, and can only get the data showing on the result page. I would like to get the raw data of an experiment when I'm on a result page, to be able to analyze it with my own tools for example. ``` **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround description:** : Users can specifically ask Kameleoon to access the raw data of an experiment, and we can provide them such data, because we do have it, we just didn't make it available to everyone easily yet\. ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user? ``` -It brings more transparency to the users, as they can see the data we are getting on their website before we transform it and display it on the result page. -It will give more flexibility to users as they will be able to manipulate the data on their end, and they might want insights we don't currently offer on the result page. ``` **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users\. ``` When user wants to analyze data of an experiment run on their website, as they love Kameleoon experiments but rather experiment with their data themselves, they will be able to get this data and do whatever they want with it. ``` **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation \/ Full Stack Experimentation \/ Feature Management \/ AI\-driven Personalization - **Product scope:** Product section and pages that will evolve \(if needed, define sections\/pages that will be out of scope\) - **Target Persona**: Which one of our target persona is going to benefit from this feature? \(Marketer \/ Developer \/ Product Manager\) - **Main updates:** - In the result page \>\> in the actions dropdown \>\> in the export section - There will be a new field, above all the others, called " type of export", with 2 options : raw \(new\) or aggregated data \(what we currently offer\) - If aggregated is selected, nothing changes, it stays the same as it is now - If raw is selected, we remove the last 2 fields \("include" , and "view by goal"\) and add a new field called "email address", where the default email will be the account one, but the user can edit this field and type his own mail if it's not the same \( as many users can use the same account \) - User validates and receives, when it's ready, either the file with the format he selected, or a link to download the file \( we're not sure yet about what's the best\) - We have not decided of a time\/size limit yet, but we might add one if needed\. ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** The goal of this topic is to add more transparency and flexibility in the analysis capacity we offer to our customers - **Success metric:** The key metric indicator will be the number of raw exports done across our customers' accounts --- ## 📄 Attached documents - **Figma file**: There won't be any Figma as it's mostly back\-end work\. - **Spec file**: We have [this draft for now ](https://navy-top-697.notion.site/Raw-data-export-209c8c9f1154408292687ca7684be935#a7f34388ab2348fa94226ab43644c07c) - **Redmine ticket**:

Title: Bot Filtering for Full Stack Experimentation
Description: Websites today are commonly visited by **bots** and **spiders** which skew event tracking and conversion data by posing as actual human visitors\. Experiment results can lose their value if numbers get inflated due to bot visits, which is why Kameleoon provides an easy solution for Full Stack customers to filter out bots with known [user agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_agent) that are listed on the actively maintained [**IAB\/ABC**](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/iab-abc-international-spiders-bots-list/) database\. > *The IAB has enlisted The Alliance for Audited Media to perform evaluation and management services associated with maintaining and publishing the industry Spider and Robot list, the use of which is required for compliance to the IAB’s Client Side Counting \(CSC\) Measurement Guidelines for “double pass” filtering\.* When tracking events with an SDK, Full Stack customers will need to simply pass their visitors' *user agent* attribute along with the other information for the bot to automatically be filtered\.

Title: Edge CDN Kits
Description: ## 📒 **Feature summary:** An Edge CDN is cloud technology that specializes in static site hosting and serverless functions\. It provides developers with a seamless way to deploy and scale their websites, web applications, and APIs\. They focus on simplifying the deployment process and optimising the performance of web projects \- ensuring fast loading times and efficient delivery to end users\. --- ## 💡 Solution benefits What value does this feature bring to the user? - **Improved website performance:** Edge CDN technologies distribute content closer to end users, reducing latency and improving website loading speeds\. This results in a better user experience and higher engagement levels\. - **Reduced bandwidth costs:** By caching content at edge server locations, edge CDNs help offload traffic from origin servers, reducing the bandwidth consumption and associated costs\. - **Enhanced scalability:** Edge CDNs offer scalable infrastructure that can handle high volumes of traffic without impacting performance\. This enables websites to accommodate sudden spikes in user activity or handle increased demand during peak periods\. - **Increased global reach:** With edge server locations distributed across the globe, edge CDNs can deliver content to users regardless of their geographical location\. This improves website accessibility and ensures consistent performance for users worldwide\. - **Improved reliability and resilience:** Edge CDNs use a distributed network of servers, reducing the risk of single points of failure\. If one edge server goes down, requests can be automatically rerouted to the nearest available server, ensuring continuous content delivery\. - **Flexibility and agility:** Edge CDNs provide flexibility in managing and delivering content\. They support dynamic content updates, enable A\/B testing, FF usage, and facilitate quick deployment of changes, allowing product teams to respond rapidly to user demands and market trends\. ## **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation \/ Full Stack Experimentation \/ Feature Management - **Product scope:** Developers

What's more, since the data is globally distributed, latency for the initial read is reduced. Compute before the cacheWhen compute happens instantly, routing decisions can be made before the cache. Title: Multi-Armed Bandit Experiments
Description: ## 🚀 Feature Summary The goal of this feature is to introduce a **Multi\-Armed Bandit** for traffic allocation in Feature Experiment's variation split\. The MAB will optimize the distribution of user traffic among different feature variations, allowing for efficient and automated decision\-making during A\/B testing and experimentation\. --- ## 😥 Problem - As a user, I face: - **Inefficient Traffic Allocation:** Challenges in determining the optimal allocation of user traffic among multiple feature variations during A\/B testing\. Manual allocation methods may result in suboptimal decisions and wasted opportunities\. - **Missed Opportunities:** Manual allocation, especially over several ongoing experiments may fail to leverage real\-time feedback from ongoing experiments, leading to missed opportunities to quickly identify and promote high\-performing variations\. - **Resource Drain:** Manual management of traffic allocation requires significant time and effort from me and my team, diverting their focus away from core tasks and slowing down the experimentation process\. - **Workaround:** None, manual intervention is a must\. ## 💡 Solution Benefits 1. **Optimized Traffic Allocation:** Intelligently adjusts the distribution of user traffic among different feature variations based on real\-time feedback\. It dynamically balances exploration \(trying out new variations\) and exploitation \(promoting successful variations\), leading to better overall performance and quicker identification of winning variations\. 1. **Quick Insights and Iteration:** Users can gain actionable insights more rapidly, allowing users to iterate and improve their products faster\. 1. **Resource Efficiency:** Eliminates the need for manual management, saving users time and effort\. Users can focus on strategic decision\-making and experiment analysis rather than manual allocation\. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/64ecaa5e8e1753c337fe0c639ccb05ccba2251d9d76e75d1b7b2877cb1fafd6a/image.png) ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/bd0f1c481e68fd13803977e89a4126be9d7b16f69caa3b5a7fe5b642f793efb6/image.png) **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management and Experiment - **Product scope:** Rollout Planner - **Target Persona**: PM - **Main updates:** A simple toggle in the experiment variation split selection\. ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** Improved conversion metrics - **Success metric:** Feature adoption, user feedback --- ## 📄 Attached documents - NA - Redmine ticket: NA

Title: Sequential testing
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` Sequential Testing allows users to continuously monitor the performance of different variations in an A/B test and make informed decisions as soon as statistically significant results are achieved, without the need to wait for a fixed sample size to be reached. ``` ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? ``` Traditional A/B testing methods often require a predetermined sample size and fixed testing duration, which can lead to inefficiencies and delayed decision-making. In many cases, users are left waiting for extended periods before they can confidently choose a winning variation or halt underperforming ones. This approach is suboptimal in scenarios where quick decisions are essential, such as optimizing conversion rates, user engagement, or revenue generation. Sequential Testing aims to address these limitations and provide a more flexible and efficient testing framework. ``` **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround description:** : Users can manually check his experiment's results on all the existing segments to see the test's result on each\. ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user? ``` -Faster Decision-Making: Sequential Testing enables users to make decisions as soon as statistically significant differences between variations emerge, reducing the time required to reach conclusive results. -Resource Efficiency: Users can optimize their testing resources by stopping underperforming variations early and reallocating traffic to more promising ones, leading to cost savings and better allocation of resources. -Improved User Experience: By quickly identifying and implementing winning variations, organizations can enhance user experience, drive better engagement, and ultimately improve key performance metrics. -Adaptive Testing: The feature adapts to the actual behavior of users, ensuring that if a significant difference exists, it will be detected with high probability while minimizing the risk of making incorrect decisions due to random fluctuations. ``` **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users\. ``` This feature can be used for each AB test. ``` **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** All packages\. - **Product scope:** Result page\. - **Target Persona**: Marketer \/ Product Manager - **Main updates:** - Addition of a toggle to choose between sequential or classic approach\. ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** The goal is to align with our competitors who offer this feature\. - **Success metric:** Number of customer running a sequential experiment\. --- ## 📄 Attached documents - **Figma file**: - **Spec file**: - **Redmine ticket**:

Title: RBAC: User Permissions for FE
Description: Pains: 1. Risk Mitigation: Without the Four\-Eyes Principle, there is a higher risk of introducing faulty or problematic features into production, leading to potential bugs, performance issues, or security vulnerabilities\. 1. Lack of Accountability: When changes to feature flags are made by a single individual, it becomes difficult to trace back and assign responsibility in case of errors or negative outcomes\. 1. Quality Assurance Challenges: In the absence of multiple reviewers, the likelihood of overlooking potential issues or gaps in feature flag configurations increases, resulting in lower overall software quality\. 1. Compliance and Governance: Organizations operating in regulated industries or following strict compliance requirements may face difficulties in meeting audit and governance standards without a robust approval process in place\. Gains: 1. Enhanced Security: By requiring the involvement of multiple authorized individuals, the Four\-Eyes Principle adds an extra layer of security, reducing the risk of unauthorized or malicious changes to feature flags\. 1. Improved Quality Control: Having multiple reviewers ensures that proposed changes undergo thorough scrutiny, catching errors, inconsistencies, or potential pitfalls early in the process, leading to higher\-quality software deployments\. 1. Shared Knowledge and Collaboration: The Four\-Eyes Principle fosters collaboration and knowledge sharing among team members\. Reviewers can provide valuable insights, suggestions, or alternative approaches to improve the feature flag configurations\. 1. Transparent Decision\-Making: With a clear approval workflow and audit trail, the decision\-making process becomes transparent and accountable, enabling stakeholders to understand who reviewed and approved each change\. 1. Compliance and Auditing: Organizations can meet regulatory and compliance requirements by having a controlled and documented approval process for feature flag changes, ensuring accountability and adherence to established guidelines\. 1. Confidence in Deployments: By implementing the Four\-Eyes Principle, users of the feature flag tool can gain confidence in their deployment process, knowing that changes are subject to thorough review and scrutiny, reducing the risk of negative impacts on end\-users\. 1. Error Detection and Prevention: Multiple sets of eyes can identify potential issues, such as conflicts with existing feature flags, incorrect configurations, or unintended consequences, minimizing the chances of introducing bugs or performance regressions\. 1. Continuous Improvement: The feedback and suggestions provided by the reviewers during the approval process can lead to iterative improvements in feature flag configurations, resulting in a more optimized and stable software system over time\. By embedding the Four\-Eyes Principle into the workflow of a feature flag tool, users can benefit from increased security, improved quality control, collaborative decision\-making, and better compliance with industry standards\. This ultimately leads to more reliable software deployments and a smoother user experience\.

Title: Technical Debt Management
Description: ## 🚀 Feature Summary Technical debt management in feature flags refers to the process of identifying, tracking, and addressing technical debt associated with feature flags within your codebase\. Over time, as new features are released and experiments conducted using feature flags, technical debt may accumulate within the codebase that becomes increasingly difficult to proactively cleanup\. --- ## 😥 Problem As a user, I face: - **Accumulated Technical Debt:** Users face challenges in managing and reducing technical debt associated with feature flags and other instances of Kameleoon's SDK, leading to code complexity and maintenance issues\. - **Time\-Consuming Manual Efforts:** The current process for identifying and addressing tech debt requires extensive manual intervention, diverting resources from other critical tasks\. - **Risk of Bugs and Errors:** Unresolved tech debt may lead to increased risks of bugs, errors, and performance issues in the application\. - **Impact on Team Efficiency:** Dealing with tech debt hampers development team productivity, slowing down feature development and experimentation\. - **Workaround:** Using filters with key dates to track flags not edited in a long time\. Still pretty manual\. ## 💡 Solution Benefits With this feature, I benefit from: - **Streamlined cleanup process:** The feature provides an simplified process to identify, track, and address tech debt related to feature flags, ensuring a cleaner and more maintainable codebase\. - **Time and Resource Savings**: Users save valuable time and effort if stale flags are highlighted for them, clearing up bandwidth for feature improvements\. - **Enhanced Code Quality:** The simple improvement helps developers improve the overall code quality, reducing the likelihood of bugs in the long\-term and enhancing application performance\. - **Faster Feature Development:** With reduced tech debt, development teams can accelerate forward with more peace of mind, and deliver new functionalities more efficiently\. ## **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management and Experiment - **Product scope:** FME Dashboard - **Target Persona**: Developers - **Main updates:** Dashboard enhancements to highlight flags that may be stale\.\. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/ca07e65981e10cdc66097697b5faab91a1c8451b1007d63a895388e8db82511b/image.png) ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - How many flags were deleted when marked as stale? - Measure the decrease in the total number of stale flags over a specific period\. --- ## 📄 Attached documents - Designs: [Figma file](https://www.figma.com/file/s2i4MS9OpfJ9RidwRgPGCM/FF_Goals%26Rollbacks?type=design&node-id=343-16064&mode=design&t=6Mm2BrOf008V64Cw-0) - Redmine ticket: NA

Title: AI Opportunity detection
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` Opportunity detector is a new feature which will be enabled for our audience customers. When an audience customer will run a test, if the test is not "winning", we will look at the test's results filtered over each of his segments. An opportunity is a subsegment of the test's targeting segment with a relative size of at least 15% of the initial segment and with a reliable positive effect over the original. We will notify the user for each opportunity we find and propose the user to duplicate the experiment to validate the opportunity. ``` ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? ``` We are trying to get the most out of an A/B test, as it can get frustrating to see an idea "loose" the test. If it turns out the experiment is actually winning on a subsegment, this can lead to personalization opportunities. ``` **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround description:** : Users can manually check his experiment's results on all the existing segments to see the test's result on each\. ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user? ``` - It brings a lot of value as we aim to get the most out of every idea which is tested and to not miss any opportunity to serve what is suiting the visitor best. ``` **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users\. ``` Every time a test is inconclusive or is worsening a KPI. ``` **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Packages with audience included\. - **Product scope:** The opportunity research will take place in the experiments result pages\. - **Target Persona**: Marketer \/ Product Manager - **Main updates:** - Addition of a loading icon to notify the user that we are searching for opportunities\. - Addition of a pop\-in if we find any opportunity\. ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** The goal is to give more value to audience and to encourage our users to engage with audience more \/ create more audience segments\. - **Success metric:** Number of customer subscribed to the audience package\. Number of audience segment created\. --- ## 📄 Attached documents - **Figma file**: [Figma](https://www.figma.com/file/WVkHeYd2NscazYjzCfftom/Opportunity-found?type=design&node-id=0-1&mode=design) - **Spec file**: - **Redmine ticket**:

"Read-only" mode for Autopromo on sub-sites
Description: ## Short Description: When setting up autopromotion campaigns, National will have the option to enable a "read\-only" mode for subsites, preventing them from making any changes to the campaign or the associated segment\. ## How will it works in practice? **For national \(meta\-site\)** - Before duplication, addition of a toggle "Forbid subsites from modifying campaign content" **For subsites:** - personalization creation page appears as usual \(including header with name, tags and segment\) - campaign "content" block is different: it cannot be edited, and is only visible in read\-only mode - segment choice and edition is locked \(thus, segment is identical to the National one\) - all actions at the bottom are the same as today \(sites can put the campaign online at their own level\)

Title: Exclusive Widgets template for the National (Meta)
Description: ## Short Description: Some "Widgets templates" will be exclusively available at the national level\. Subsites can effortlessly inherit these widgets for national\-level campaigns, but when they create their own campaigns on their subsites, these templates won't appear, ensuring they're reserved for national campaigns only\. ## How will it works in practice? **For National:** - Addition of an "Exclusive National template" option \(in the widget template interface\) - Ability to select all widgets templates \(no change with current situation\) **For subsites:** - Subsites will inherit widgets template coming from the Nation \(when used in duplicated campaigns\) - But such widget templates will be completely invisible for subsites, which means that: - "Exclusive National widget templates" won't appear in the Widget Dashboard - Subsites won't be able to create a new campaign using an "Exclusive national widget template" - Duplication of a campaign using an "exclusive nation widget template" will be impossible\.

Title: Enhancement of Autopromotion Duplication
Description: The mechanism for duplicating a national campaign to the subsites can take some time\. It was not clear when the process was completed and whether any errors occurred during the duplication process\. The goal of this feature is to enhance this mechanism\. Now, a real\-time progress bar shows the duplication progress, and when an error occurs, the user is immediately notified \(along with the names of the subsites where the error occurred\)\.

Title: Update of BPCE daily export
Description: BPCE receives every day and every week a report of all created personalizations\. In the export, you will now find a new column named 'Meta Personalization ID' for each personalization\. This column will display the ID of the meta personalization originating from the national level, which triggered the automatic duplication on subsites\. This addition provides better visibility and tracking of your personalizations across different levels of your campaigns\.

Title: Experiment-Level Global Code
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** Describe what the feature does\. ``` This feature allows Developers to easily incorporate and manage experiment-specific global code directly within the experiment. By providing a dedicated global code field, it enables the simulation of global scripts and facilitates the inclusion of temporary code for targeting purposes. The added benefit of automatic code removal upon experiment stopping ensures a clean and efficient process, contributing to overall performance optimization. ``` ## 😥 Problem **Problem statement:** What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? ``` As a developer, when I want to implement experiment-specific global scripts or include temporary code for precise targeting in experiments, I encounter the following problems: Lack of a dedicated space within each experiment for global code management that only serves that experiment. The only way is to add that code to the global tracking script which has several drawbacks : - no possibility to simulate that code, - cluttered and less organized setup as the global script contains both temporary experiment code and tracking code for goals conversions..), resulting in potential performance issues and a lack of code cleanliness. ``` **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround description:** adding that code to the Global Tracking Script ## 💡 Solution **Key benefits**: What value does this feature bring to the user? ``` This feature streamlines the development process by providing a dedicated space for experiment-specific global code. Developers can now confidently implement and test code within the scope of each experiment, minimizing the risk of introducing bugs into the production environment. The separation of experiment code from the global tracking script eliminates the need for risky workarounds, contributing to a smoother and more reliable development experience. ``` **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users\. ``` When the developer wants to add temporary code (e.g., for targeting purposes), they want to seamlessly integrate and execute that code within the experiment setup, ensuring it is processed by Kameleoon before any targeting takes place. This enables developers to efficiently include temporary code for targeting purposes directly within the experiment, ensuring it gets executed by Kameleoon at the appropriate stage. This streamlines the development process and ensures precise targeting without compromising on the organization and execution of the code. ``` **✏️ Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation - **Product scope:** Code Editor - **Target Persona**: Developers ## 🎯 **Measuring Success** **Feature Adoption Rate:** - We will measure how quickly users adopt the new feature\. A high adoption rate may indicate that the feature is well\-received and addresses user needs\. **Performance improvements:** - Evaluate the cleanliness and organization of code by measuring the reduction of code within the global tracking script\. Measure what's the average size of the global script today versus in about 1\-3 months after the feature is released\. --- ## 📄 Attached documents - **Figma file**: optional \(paste link\) - **Spec file**: optional \(paste link\) - **Redmine ticket**: mandatory \(paste link\) - **Image:** mandatory, to illustrate the topic

If it’s systematically impacted by a treatment, CUPED becomes invalid\. - The CUPED method above only removes variance that can be accounted for linearly\. Title: Scheduled XML file import

**User Feedback:**

- Setting a specific time for importing XML files on an e-commerce website's recommendations block is crucial for ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of product recommendations. Here's why:Freshness of Data: By setting a specific time for importing XML files, the system ensures that the latest updates from suppliers or product databases are included in the recommendations. This freshness of data is essential for providing customers with up-to-date information about products available for purchase.Relevance to Customers: Customers expect relevant recommendations based on their current interests and preferences. Importing XML files at specific times allows the system to incorporate the most recent data, thereby increasing the relevance of product recommendations. This relevance enhances the overall user experience and increases the likelihood of conversion.Competitive Advantage: In the highly competitive e-commerce landscape, staying ahead with the latest products and offerings is crucial. By importing XML files at specific times, the e-commerce website can ensure that its recommendations feature showcases the newest products, giving it a competitive edge over other platforms that may not update their recommendations as frequently.Accurate Inventory Management: Setting a specific time for importing XML files also aids in accurate inventory management. By regularly updating product information, including availability and pricing, the system can prevent recommending out-of-stock items or displaying outdated prices, which can lead to customer frustration and loss of sales.Optimized Performance: Importing XML files at specific times allows for better resource allocation and system performance optimization. By scheduling imports during off-peak hours or times of low website traffic, the system can minimize disruption to the user experience while ensuring that recommendations are continuously updated and available when customers visit the website.In conclusion, setting a specific time for importing XML files is essential for maintaining the freshness, relevance, and accuracy of product recommendations on an e-commerce website. By prioritizing timely updates, the platform can provide customers with a superior shopping experience, gain a competitive advantage, and drive increased sales and customer satisfaction.

Title: Custom teams
Description: ## 📒 **Feature short description:** The updates improve team management in Kameleoon, allowing users to assign teams to web pages, manage multiple teams, and streamline user management\. The campaigns dashboard now displays only relevant campaigns, with admins retaining full visibility\. Campaign creation ensures coherence between teams and properties, with exceptions for admins\. These changes enhance efficiency and organization within the platform\. ## ⁉️ Problem Statement The problem we aim to address is the lack of robust team management functionality within the Kameleoon platform\. Currently, there are limitations in specifying team ownership for web pages, managing multiple teams, and efficiently assigning users to teams\. This lack of flexibility hampers workflow organization and can lead to confusion and inefficiencies, especially in projects involving multiple teams or complex campaign structures\. Additionally, there is a need to ensure coherence between team assignments and campaign properties to maintain consistency and streamline campaign management\. Overall, the goal is to enhance team management capabilities to improve collaboration, organization, and workflow efficiency within the Kameleoon platform\. ## 🔑 Key Features 1. **Customization of Snippet with Tag:** 1. Allow customers to include an optional property in the Kameleoon snippet indicating the entitled team for the page\. 1. Investigate the feasibility of defining multiple teams with Aleksey\. If feasible, assess the effort required\. 1. **Page Team:** 1. Rename "Page Team" to "Users\." 1. Introduce a "Team" column to specify user affiliations\. 1. Enable super admin users to assign teams via a unique action in the options menu\. 1. **Creation of Team Interface:** 1. Implement a quick\-to\-implement pop\-up or page\. 1. Enable activation of the "team" feature\. 1. Provide functionality to list, create, and edit teams, including name, tag key, and optional description\. 1. **Addition of Users:** 1. Integrate a team dropdown during user addition for super admin users if the "teams" feature is activated\. 1. **Campaigns Dashboard Adaptation:** 1. Display only campaigns managed by the user's team, with an exception for project admins who see all project campaigns\. 1. Include a team filter in the sidebar for admins\. 1. Add a "team" column to the campaigns dashboard for admins\. 1. **Campaign Creation:** 1. Implement a check to ensure coherence between the "team property" on the URL and the user's team when creating a campaign\. Display an error message if inconsistent\. 1. Title: Barrier-free accessibility
User_Notes:
---
**User Feedback:**
- Pain Point: From mid-2025, websites and apps will be legally required to be barrier-free. This is regulated by the Barrier-Free Accessibility Strengthening Act (BFSG). The Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) implements the EU directive of the European Accessibility Act (EAA) so that standardised rules on accessibility apply throughout Europe. The regulations are based on the European standard EN 301 549, which in turn is largely based on the international guidelines for accessible web content (WCAG). e.g. sufficient contrast between foreground and background colour, links and buttons operable via the keyboard, screen reader compatibility of a website, etc. Even if the website offers this accessibility on its live site, there is still a risk that the variant of an experiment or personalisation will not fulfil it. Such a design can have legal consequences and penalties. Solution: There are various features in Kameleoon that check for accessibility when changes are made. The contrast check of colours in new editors is a first step and a good example of this.
- The customer wants more AI in the Graphic Editor. There is currently support for the barrier-free accessibility of headings, for example. One suggestion is that the AI should support where it is best to place the element. A possible suggestion is that the place where the element is best placed is highlighted in color.
- great differentiators with enterprise groups.

This lack of control forces users to manually adjust content every time they generate text, leading to inconsistencies in tone, compliance issues, and inefficiencies\. ### **Feature Principle** ✨ **Global AI Content Generation Customizations** introduce a centralized system for defining **rules and constraints** for AI\-generated content across all AI\-powered features in **AI Copilot**\. This allows users to **predefine guidelines** that shape AI outputs according to their brand, compliance requirements, and business needs\. ### **Key Functionalities** ✅ **Tone of Voice Configuration** – Users can select or create predefined tones of voice that the AI must follow across all content\. ✅ **Restricted Keywords & Compliance Rules** – Users can specify words or phrases that AI should avoid to ensure brand safety and regulatory compliance\. ✅ **Prompt Templates & Structure Constraints** – Users can enforce predefined content structures to maintain consistency across different AI use cases\. ✅ **Protected Content Parameters** – Users can define elements that AI should not modify \(e\.g\., product names, legal disclaimers\)\. ✅ **CSS & Content Exclusion Rules** – Allows users to exclude specific UI elements or text sections from AI processing\. ✅ **Pre\-Treatment & Post\-Treatment Scripts** – Supports customization with JavaScript to preprocess or refine AI\-generated content before display\. ### **Expected Impact** 🚀 **More Control Over AI Outputs** – Ensures AI\-generated content aligns with business, legal, and branding guidelines\. 📈 **Efficiency Gains** – Reduces the need for repetitive manual edits by enforcing global content rules\. ⚡ **Scalability & Consistency** – Provides a standardized AI configuration across AI Experiments, Graphical Editor, and Widget Studio, ensuring uniform output across the product\.

Title: Synthetic control group
Description: A synthetic control in the context of A\/B testing on the web is a method of analysis that is used to create an artificial control group when a real control group cannot be obtained due to limitations in the experiment\. Typically, a synthetic control is used when it is difficult or impossible to conduct a full randomized experiment with a real control group\. This typically uses a statistical method that combines data from other groups, segments, or time to “simulate” the behavior that the control group might have if it existed\. It is easy to sell to a team launching the projects with 100% on Variation\. For example: some marketing activities where test is going to diverted and client can not sacrifice traffic for AB tests and still wants so see what additional income they had\.

Title: ✨ AI Assistant - Response Progress
Description: ### **Problem Statement** Currently, when a user makes a request in **KAI \(chatbot\)** that takes a long time to process \(up to **30 seconds**\), there is **no clear feedback** on what is happening\. This lack of transparency can lead to frustration, confusion, and potential drop\-offs\. ### **Feature Principle** Introduce **real\-time request progress feedback** to keep users informed when a request is undergoing multiple processing steps\. This mirrors how **ChatGPT handles complex queries**, reassuring users that their request is actively being processed rather than failing or stalling\. ### **Key Functionalities** ✅ **Step\-by\-Step Progress Indicator** – Show a dynamic progress message or animation indicating where the request is in the pipeline\. ✅ **Descriptive Status Updates** – Display messages like: - *"Analyzing your request\.\.\."* - *"Retrieving relevant information\.\.\."* - \*"Finalizing response\.\.\."\* ✅ **Adaptive Feedback** – Adjust the messaging based on expected response time, reducing perceived wait time\. ✅ **Fallback Mechanism** – If processing exceeds a critical threshold, provide a friendly notification or alternative action\. ### **Expected Impact** 🚀 **Better User Experience** – Reduces frustration by keeping users informed about what’s happening behind the scenes\. 📈 **Higher Engagement & Retention** – Users are less likely to abandon the chatbot during long processing times\. ⚡ **Enhanced Perceived Speed** – Even if a request takes long, clear status updates make the wait feel shorter\.

Title: AI suggestions - Unified text improvements
Description: ### **Problem Statement** Currently, textual improvement suggestions are generated on a per\-page basis for product pages, which can lead to redundant efforts when multiple pages contain similar or identical content needing revision\. This approach can be inefficient and lacks a quantitative dimension to help prioritize which changes are most impactful\. ### **Feature Principle** When identical or very similar text improvements are detected across multiple pages \(for instance, dozens of pages sharing the same snippet\), the system should offer a single consolidated solution for all those pages, with two possible approaches: 1. **LLM\-Driven \(Automatic\)**: The LLM automatically selects the best improvement proposal based on context and text quality across those pages\. 1. **User\-Driven \(Tabular View\)**: A table displays different potential improvements, allowing the user to choose the most appropriate one based on quantitative criteria such as: - **Readability Score** \(e\.g\., Flesch\-Kincaid\) - **SEO Impact Estimation** \(e\.g\., presence of relevant keywords\) - **Estimated Conversion Rate** \(if available, based on historical data or industry benchmarks\) - **Contextual Relevance** \(a rating of how well the text aligns with the page’s intent and best writing practices\) #### **Quantitative Data to Include** - **Frequency of Occurrence**: The number of pages containing the text snippet to justify a single consolidated proposal\. - **Comparative Analysis**: Evaluation of different proposals regarding readability, SEO potential, and historical performance\. - **User Engagement Impact**: Potential effect of the changes on metrics like time on page or bounce rate\. ### **Expected Impact** - **Reduced Redundancy**: Centralized management of similar text improvements across multiple pages, ensuring a more consistent user experience\. - **Increased Relevance**: Quantitative data helps users make more informed decisions about which improvements to apply\. - **Productivity Gains**: Users can swiftly apply the best suggestions to multiple pages without addressing each page individually\.

Title: Custom Bucketing Key
Description: A **custom bucketing key** will allow you to control how users are consistently assigned to variations based on a user\-defined identifier rather than the default one \(visitor code\)\. This is especially useful when your customers such as agencies \(or certain applications\) need to group users differently than the default logic — for example, by account ID, session ID, device ID, or any other relevant key in your business logic\. By using a custom bucketing key, you ensure that the same entity \(e\.g\., a company or group\) always gets the same variation, even if individual users change or switch devices\. It’s also helpful in B2B contexts where features should be rolled out at the **account level**, not the user level\. This flexibility gives you greater targeting precision, consistency, and control in your rollouts and experiments\.
